thread:
leo - Hey team - our prod app started getting 429s yesterday evening. Dashboard shows "0 / 1,000,000 tokens remaining" but our billing cycle is day 12 of 30. We were on Starter (500k/mo) and upgraded to Growth (1M/mo) on day 8. When do the extra tokens actually apply? Did we lose tokens when we upgraded? Also saw this header on one response: `X-Redwood-Quota-Reset: 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z` — not sure if that's right.

maya - Sorry to hear that, leo. Can you DM me your org id and one of the failing request IDs? Also which API key (org vs user) you used. 429 likely means monthly quota is exhausted, but we'll confirm.

leo - Org: org_9xw2. Sample request id: req_abc123. We use an org key. I can paste curl if helpful.

maya - Please paste the curl (no secret keys) and the response headers you saw. Also which timezone you expect the reset in — are you in PST? :thinking_face:

leo - PST. Here is the curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer org_XXXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Response headers snip:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-Remaining-Tokens: 0
X-Redwood-Quota-Reset: 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z
X-Request-ID: req_abc123
```

ben - Looping in billing. Quick answer: reset timing is tied to your billing cycle start day and is evaluated in UTC at 00:00. Upgrades increase your quota ceiling immediately, but how the extra tokens are applied to the current cycle varies: we normally prorate remaining days and credit the additional token allotment into your current cycle immediately. However, sometimes the background proration worker can be delayed and the UI may still show old numbers until it finishes. We'll check account history.

carla - From the infra side: two separate controls here — short-term rate limits (requests/sec, token-bucket) and long-term monthly quota (token budget). Getting a 429 with X-Redwood-Remaining-Tokens: 0 indicates the monthly budget is depleted, not necessarily a requests/sec spike. The token-bucket for bursts won't help if the monthly pool is empty.

carla - Diagnostic steps: please run this to capture headers on a failing call and paste output:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer org_XXXX" -H "Org: org_9xw2" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"debug"}'
```
We need X-Redwood-Quota-Reset and X-Redwood-Remaining-Tokens from the response. Also confirm the account created the subscription on which day (billing-start-date).

leo - Billing-start-date is 2025-10-01. Ran the curl and the headers above are from the failing response. Happy to share more.

billing-bot - billing-sync-job started for org_9xw2 at 1778001300.

ben - I checked the ledger: you upgraded on 2025-10-08 14:12 UTC. Proration job was queued and completed at 1778001355, but due to a rounding edge-case the computed additional tokens for the remaining 22 days were applied as 0 in our internal cache for a subset of accounts. We're investigating.

maya - TL;DR: upgrade should have given you the extra tokens immediately, but there was a proration processing bug that left remaining tokens at the old level briefly. We're going to manually credit the missing tokens for the current cycle while billing fixes the batch job.

carla - Also note: the dashboard can sometimes show cached usage until the usage-aggregation job runs (every ~5 minutes). But the 0 remaining looks like the proration rounding issue ben mentioned, not just a cache lag.

leo - Thanks — can you restore now? We're throttled in prod.

ben - I've applied a manual credit of +500,000 tokens to org_9xw2 for the remainder of the cycle (ticket #BILL-4521). You should see remaining tokens increase within 1 minute. If you still get 429s include X-Request-ID and we'll trace.

billing-bot - billing-sync-job completed for org_9xw2 at 1778001355.

leo - Confirmed, traffic is normal again. Remaining header now shows X-Redwood-Remaining-Tokens: 489432. Thanks!

maya - Glad that helped. Internal follow-up: billing to fix proration rounding (ben) and infra to add a dashboard cache invalidation on manual credits (carla). I'll keep this thread open until the root cause is closed. :thumbsup:

ben - We'll push a fix to the proration worker and run a retroactive migration for any affected accounts. ETA 48h, will update BILL-4521.

carla - For future reference: if you need immediate extra capacity we can also enable a temporary burst override (short-lived) to cover sudden traffic spikes while billing catches up. That's useful for migrations or launches.

leo - Appreciate it. Leaving this thread open for updates on the billing ticket.
